`run_local_command_modern_version` takes a new `is_detached_from_terminal` option, which runs the child in its own session so it inherits neither the caller's controlling terminal nor its process group.

Without it, a child that reaches the terminal can freeze the process that ran it. Redirecting stdio is not enough to prevent this: the `claude` CLI opens `/dev/tty` directly even with stdin on `DEVNULL` and stdout/stderr on pipes, and it restores terminal modes while handling the SIGTERM this helper sends when a command overruns its timeout. Because a `tcsetattr` from a process group that is not the terminal's foreground group makes the kernel deliver SIGTTOU to that whole group, the caller is stopped along with the child it was trying to kill. This is what wedged a workspace's system interface: it runs under supervisord inside a tmux pane, so it and everything it spawns sit in a background process group on the pane's terminal.

The option is off by default. Detaching also puts the child out of reach of an interactive Ctrl-C, which a CLI relies on to take its children down with it, so this stays a deliberate choice made by long-running services rather than a change of behaviour for every caller.
